brief.problem_or_goal: Discuss the observed trade-off between world knowledge and problem-solving abilities in recent smaller LLMs.
brief.context: An archived Reddit post from 2025-05-02 discusses observations about the performance of various LLMs, specifically noting a potential decline in world knowledge despite improvements in coding and problem-solving benchmarks for newer, smaller models.
brief.motivation: Understanding if there's a general trend of sacrificing world knowledge for improved problem-solving in smaller LLMs is crucial for users selecting models for diverse tasks.
brief.desired_response: A discussion exploring the source author's observations, potential reasons for this trend, and whether other enthusiasts have noticed similar patterns or have strategies for evaluating these trade-offs.
brief.speaker_relationship_to_source: reader of archived source; no claim of personally running reported tests

facts.text: The source author observed a trend where newer small models, despite higher benchmark scores and claims of equivalence to older, larger models, exhibit worse world knowledge than their larger predecessors and often worse than lower-benchmarking models of similar sizes.
facts.evidence_quote: I've noticed a trend where despite benchmark scores going up and companies claiming that their new small models are equivalent to older much bigger models, world knowledge of these new smaller models is worse than their larger predecessors, and often times worse than lower benchmarking models of similar sizes.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: The source author uses a set of private test questions covering coding, engineering problem solving, system threat modelling, and specific knowledge questions on topics like radio protocols, technical standards, local geography, history, and landmarks.
facts.evidence_quote: I have a set of private test questions that exercise coding, engineering problem solving, system threat modelling, and also ask specific knowledge questions on a variety of topics ranging from radio protocols and technical standards to local geography, history, and landmarks.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: New models like Qwen 3 and GLM-4-0414 are described as vastly better at coding and problem solving than older models, but their knowledge is no better and sometimes worse than some other similar-sized older models.
facts.evidence_quote: New models like Qwen 3 and GLM-4-0414 are vastly better at coding and problem solving than older models, but their knowledge is no better than older models and actually worse than some other similar sized older models.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: Qwen 3 8B reportedly has considerably worse world knowledge in the author's tests than older models like Llama 3.1 8B and Gemma 2 9B.
facts.evidence_quote: For example, Qwen 3 8B has considerably worse world knowledge in my tests than old models like Llama 3.1 8B and Gemma 2 9B.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: Qwen 3 14B reportedly has much worse world knowledge than older weaker benchmarking models like Phi 4 and Gemma 3 12B.
facts.evidence_quote: Likewise, Qwen 3 14B has much worse world knowledge than older weaker benchmarking models like Phi 4 and Gemma 3 12B.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: Granite 3.3 has slightly better coding/problem solving but slightly worse knowledge than Granite 3.2.
facts.evidence_quote: On a similar note, Granite 3.3 has slightly better coding/problem solving but slightly worse knowledge than Granite 3.2.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: Llama 4 Maverick has superb world knowledge, much better than Qwen 3 235B-A22, and slightly better than DeepSeek V3 in the author's tests, but its coding and problem solving abilities are mediocre.
facts.evidence_quote: Llama 4 Maverick has superb world knowledge, much better than Qwen 3 235B-A22, and actually slightly better than DeepSeek V3 in my tests, but its coding and problem solving abilities are mediocre.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: The source author guesses that the trade-off is due to training data for new models having more problem solving content and proportionately less knowledge-dense content.
facts.evidence_quote: My guess is that this is because the training data for new models has more problem solving content and so proportionately less knowledge dense content.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement
